- **Change:** `if not (0 <= value < 100):` is now `if not (0 <= value <= 100):`.

The old check rejected 100 as out of range, so the parser returned `None` and routing fell back to the requested model. The JSON-path parser at line 1294 already used `<= 100`, so only the plain-text path was affected.

content.text:
The root cause was a misspelled header name in `anthrouter/http_util.py`, line 120, in the `_RATELIMIT_HEADERS` tuple. I made the one-word fix there and didn't run the tests.

The entry looked for `anthropic-ratelimit-request-remaining` (singular "request"), but Anthropic sends `anthropic-ratelimit-requests-remaining`. `parse_ratelimit_headers` therefore never found the header, so `requests_remaining` was never set. The DB record path (`db.py` reads `rl.get('requests_remaining')`) and the transport call were already correct, which is why the token windows kept working.

The change was `('requests_remaining', 'anthropic-ratelimit-request-remaining')` to `('requests_remaining', 'anthropic-ratelimit-requests-remaining')`.

The diff touches only those two source lines, and I didn't change any existing tests.
